source.title: On the Difficulty of Warm-Starting Neural Network Training
source.authors: Jordan T. Ash; Ryan P. Adams

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests how sequential warm-start training on natural image data changes held-out accuracy, a setting not covered by the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports held-out accuracy for warm-started and randomly initialized models. Other regularization and hyperparameter findings are described in text or figures; no separate numeric rows are extracted for those here.
record.test_reason: Table 1 contains a test of V3: randomly initialized ResNet-18 models outperform randomly initialized fully connected MLPs on all three image datasets with both optimizers. The main warm-start intervention fits no version. The optimizer comparison uses one shared, fixed learning rate rather than the tuning protocol named in V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: warm starting generally harms neural-network generalization despite similar training performance; tested hyperparameters can close the gap while losing the training-time advantage, and shrink-and-perturb can restore accuracy while retaining speed in the studied sequential settings. The blanket wording should acknowledge the near-equal SVHN ResNet–Adam accuracies and the authors' qualification that transfer-learning outcomes depend on source, target, and available target data.
record.recipe_differences: The study compares sequential warm-start training with fresh random initialization, rather than testing the claim versions' interventions or measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported gap varies by architecture, dataset, optimizer, and the fraction of data used in the first training round. Regularization and learning-rate/batch-size choices can alter the gap; the text says these did not resolve it while preserving warm-start time benefits.

fits_no_version.finding: Warm starting generally lowers neural-network validation accuracy despite similar final training performance; logistic regression is described as showing no significant damage.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sequential warm starting can impair generalization even when successive training samples come from the same distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: At the shared fixed learning rate, Adam gives higher validation accuracy than SGD for every ResNet and MLP random-initialization comparison, whereas SGD gives higher accuracy for logistic regression.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer rankings depend on architecture under a shared fixed learning rate; these results do not establish rankings after optimizer-specific tuning.

record.peer_reviewed: 34th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2020)
record.problems: Table 1 reports validation accuracy rather than a direct training-test error gap; it does not test random-label memorization. Experiments use five runs in the described settings, and the paper states that it uses no data augmentation or learning-rate schedules unless specified.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows beyond Table 1. Hyperparameter sweeps, regularization results, and shrink-and-perturb results are described in figures or appendix tables, but they concern the warm-start intervention rather than a listed claim version.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization under the same recipe.

The contribution of local connectivity specifically; learned sparse local connections; initialization from a trained convolutional network; MNIST. The ResNet–tanh-MLP comparison changes several architectural properties together.

Optimizer comparisons after learning-rate and schedule tuning, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, optimizer switching, and word-level language modeling. Table 1 fixes the same learning rate at 0.001 for both optimizers.
Batch-size penalties under fixed epoch budgets and their removal with adapted recipes. The batch-size sweep instead trains to convergence and examines warm-start accuracy and time.
Dropout interventions and their dependence on training-set size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Removing examples selected by label-memorization influence versus random removal.

record.verdict_notes: All Table 1 numbers are transcribed correctly. V3 verdicts use the recorded random-initialization baselines across architectures, not the warm-start values. The observed states for V3 require the comparison restructuring specified in row_fixes. These comparisons establish an architectural performance difference without isolating its cause.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization under the same recipe.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance under the tuning conditions in the version.
Large-versus-small batch performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
